main_issue: Whether items like D's prayer bracelet and B's earrings may be worn if covered and not visible, under the new no-visible-jewellery rule, before the area manager visits tomorrow

A-B.evidence: B objected that A made them take earrings off (T4, T6); A conceded 'If it's covered... it's fine. That goes for everyone' (T8); B replied 'Right' (T9).

A-C.evidence: C said a plaster would work since the rule is 'not visible' (T7); A accepted covering for everyone (T8); C said 'Clear' (T12).

A-D.evidence: D asked 'Can I just cover it?' (T2); A first questioned it (T3) then allowed covering (T8); D confirmed 'I'll cover it' (T14).

B-C.evidence: C backed B's plaster idea (T7); B agreed 'Right' (T9) and C said 'Clear' (T12).

B-D.evidence: Both favour covering items (T2, T6), and both accepted the covering agreement (T9, T14), but they did not address each other.

C-D.evidence: C supports covering as meeting the rule (T7); D says 'I'll cover it' (T14); no direct exchange.
